query: How many nodes/samples are needed to detect typical ablation effect sizes (e.g., 0.5%–2% accuracy) at 80% power, and what multiple-testing correction should we apply?

response.query: How many nodes/samples are needed to detect typical ablation effect sizes (e.g., 0.5%–2% accuracy) at 80% power, and what multiple-testing correction should we apply?
response.answer: To detect 0.5%–2% accuracy changes at 80% power, typically 100–200 samples are needed. Apply Bonferroni correction for multiple testing.

Studies increasingly support the idea that fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLI) offers superior tumor detection contrast, but conventional methods are limited by low frame rates and high computational load. Combining fluorescence imaging with Spatial Frequency Domain Imaging (SFDI) can improve detection of fluorescent chemotherapeutics at tumor sites and enable marker-less identification of cancerous tissue. To recapitulate this biology, the murine KPC8060 model has been developed to mimic clinical metastatic PDAC disease and represents a preclinical model with fidelity to human disease for robust detection and tracking of CHCs. Session 12: Translational Fluorescence Lifetime-Based Molecular Imaging I. Macroscale fluorescence lifetime imaging (MFLI) offers higher sensitivity and specificity for tumor detection than intensity-based imaging, but faces challenges due to low light levels, short lifetimes, and near-infrared (NIR) detection. Clinical fluorescence lifetime (FLT) imaging for bone and soft tissue tumor margin identification.

results.content: See *Data.CMS.gov,* Medicare Shared Savings Program, Accountable Care Organizations, Public Use File (by performance year, for PY 2025), available at *https://data.cms.gov/​medicare-shared-savings-program/​accountable-care-organizations.*. Message to the Quality Payment Program listserv on January 4, 2025, entitled “The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is Soliciting Stakeholder Recommendations for Potential Consideration of New Specialty Measure Sets and/or Revisions to the Existing Specialty Measure Sets for the 2026 Performance Year of the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS).”. Section 101(b) of the Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015 (MACRA) sunset the Medicare EHR Incentive Program for Eligible Professionals, set forth at section 1848(o) of the Act. As discussed previously, section 1848(o)(2) of the Act has been incorporated into the MIPS Promoting Interoperability performance category's requirements via section 1848(q)(2)(B)(iv) of the Act. See CY 2017 Quality Payment Program final rule (81 FR 77018 and 77019) for more information regarding the sunsetting of the Medicare EHR Incentive Program for Eligible Professionals.
